issue.title: privacy model: its download ignores Settings' Proxy (fails where a proxy is the only way out)
issue.body:
# privacy model: its download ignores Settings' Proxy

## What happens

On a machine whose only way out is a proxy, Settings → Privacy's local model fails to turn on:

```
downloading pf-serve: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/releases/download/pf-v1/pf-serve-linux-amd64.zip:
Get "https://release-assets.githubusercontent.com/github-production-release-asset/…":
net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

Settings' Proxy is set (`socks5h://192.168.1.233:1081`) and works — the very same URL through it
downloads in 6 seconds. Turning the model on again fails the same way, this time as a plain
`dial tcp <github ip>:443: i/o timeout`, so the request never goes near the proxy.

The model (huggingface.co) would fail the same way on such a network, so the feature cannot be
turned on at all.

## Why

`internal/pii/fetch.go` builds its client at package init:

```go
var client = func() *http.Client {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
}()
```

`netproxy.Install()` — which sets `http.DefaultTransport.Proxy = netproxy.Func`, the thing that makes
every other request of magpie's follow Settings' Proxy — runs later, from `main`
(`internal/cli/main.go`). The clone is made before it, so it keeps `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`,
which in the app and in the container has nothing to read. Both downloads therefore go direct,
whatever Settings say. (`source.Do` still asks mirrors when it can, but the zip's only mirror is
`gh-proxy`, which is behind `MAGPIE_MIRRORS=on`, so it changes nothing here.)

## Fix

`internal/update/update.go` already has the shape for exactly this:

```go
func proxied() http.RoundTripper {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func
	return netproxy.Dispatch(t)
}
```

so `internal/pii/fetch.go` can do the same (with `github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/netproxy`
imported):

```go
var client = func() *http.Client {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func // Settings' Proxy, as every other request of magpie's
	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
}()
```

Then both downloads follow Settings' Proxy (and its LAN bypass), `MAGPIE_MIRRORS=on` still gives the
`gh-proxy` fallback, and the checksums stay as they are — a mirror or a proxy is only the way there.

## Workaround (no rebuild)

Put the two files where the download would have put them, then turn the model on again — it is
judged by what is on disk, so no restart is needed:

```
<cache>/privacy-filter/pf-v1-linux-amd64/   ← the zip's contents, pf-serve executable
<cache>/privacy-filter/privacy-filter-q8-80efc1803eda.gguf
```

where `<cache>` is `~/.cache/magpie` (app, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` respected) or `/config/cache/magpie`
(the container image). The zip is `pf-serve-linux-amd64.zip` from the `pf-v1` release
(sha256 `b172f39b2b5446cb92ef14f996b65157f5e1c0e4e673ee9c61a0214cc67c78af`); the model is
`privacy-filter-q8.gguf` at revision `935d8688`
(sha256 `80efc1803eda7c095a79741d2008c07e2e0a57b01bac8825fbeb448fd097998c`, 1637572192 bytes).

## Environment

magpie v0.1.1471, server edition (the container image: `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/config/cache`),
linux-amd64, behind a proxy-only network.

## Patch

```diff
diff --git a/internal/pii/fetch.go b/internal/pii/fetch.go
index ed23cb59..ee85637b 100644
--- a/internal/pii/fetch.go
+++ b/internal/pii/fetch.go
@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@ import (
 	"sync/atomic"
 	"time"
 
+	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/netproxy"
 	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/source"
 )
 
@@ -33,6 +34,9 @@ var dl struct {
 // whose server doesn't answer by the header timeout.
 var client = func() *http.Client {
 	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
+	// through Settings' Proxy as every other request of magpie's is: the
+	// clone is made before netproxy.Install sets it on http.DefaultTransport
+	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func
 	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
 	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
 }()
```

comments.body:
Delivered on `fix/pii-download-proxy` ([55dfe0a5](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/55dfe0a5), skygunner's fork, on upstream/main 1b039a3c) — your diagnosis and fix shape, credited as found: the client's transport now asks `netproxy.Func` and goes through `netproxy.Dispatch`, exactly the `proxied()` shape `internal/update/update.go` already had, so both downloads (pf-serve's zip and the model) follow Settings' Proxy however late Install ran.

Red before: `TestDownloadFollowsTheSettingsProxy` stands your network up — a fake release host whose only route is the counting proxy — and on the old code the download bypassed it entirely (the proxy saw nothing) while still succeeding on a direct line, which is exactly how this stayed hidden on networks where direct mostly works; after, the proxy is the only way in and the one asked. The proxy is an http hop standing in for your `socks5h` (`netproxy.Parse`/`Func` take both); no real model was downloaded, the zip is bytes the test makes.

Run: `go test ./internal/pii -count=1` (17 ok), gofmt, go vet, windows/amd64 build. One housekeeping note, as with my #3531 last round: this commit was made on the same working branch as my #2741 fix before splitting (my slip, no force-push) — this fix alone is the branch pushed here; #2741's alone remains `fix/commandcode-replay-reasoning` @ 741237cf. The two touch disjoint files and cherry-pick alone.

I’m seeing a similar failure on **macOS with Magpie v0.1.1672**, which may be related to this issue.

In **Settings → Privacy → Find with a local model**, both models fail to download:

- `QuantumNous/astrlink-guard` → `int8/model_int8.onnx`
- `LocalAI-io/privacy-filter-GGUF` → `privacy-filter-q8.gguf` at revision `935d86882f4b5dc6e0eef05aae48ae5ba0a82a7a`

Across retries, I’ve seen:

```text
EOF
```

```text
tls: failed to verify certificate: x509:
certificate is valid for *.facebook.com, [...], not huggingface.co
```

```text
net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

Some diagnostic findings:

- An external proxy captures Magpie’s outbound connection. Its logs confirm that the connection is routed through the proxy and that the TCP connection and TLS handshake **to the proxy server** succeed.
- Using `curl` with an explicit HTTP proxy against the exact same download URLs works: the ONNX file downloads completely, and the GGUF URL returns HTTP 200 after following redirects. I did not download the entire GGUF file.
- Requests without an explicit HTTP proxy fail during TLS negotiation. Local DNS results were suspicious; connecting to an address obtained from an independent DNS lookup returned the expected HTTP 302 redirect.

This may be consistent with the downloader resolving the hostname locally before an external proxy captures the connection, while an explicit HTTP proxy takes a different resolution path. I haven’t confirmed that mechanism or verified whether the initialization-order bug described above is still present in v0.1.1672.

Has the proposed fix been merged into an official release? If so, could you point me to the first version containing it?

是上游自己修的，不在已发布的 release 里（截至现在）：上游 `3a89dd53`（`pii: the masking model downloads through magpie's proxy, and from hf-mirror when huggingface.co fails`，commit 里署名 "hh0592821 on Discord"，即你在 Discord 的那份报告）已落在 main 上并打了 `v0.1.1686` 的 tag，但 **`v0.1.1686` 还没有对应的 GitHub release**——目前最新的已发布 release 是 `v0.1.1685`，它不含这个修复。你用的 `v0.1.1672` 更早，所以还在旧路径上：下载客户端在包加载时就克隆了 `http.DefaultTransport`，那时 `netproxy.Install` 还没把代理装进去，克隆下来的只认 `ProxyFromEnvironment`，而从 Dock 启动的应用环境里没有 `HTTPS_PROXY`，于是走直连，撞上被污染的 huggingface.co 解析（`*.facebook.com` 的证书就是这个形状）。

几点对着你的现象说：

- 你观察到的“外部代理捕获了 magpie 的出站连接、到代理的 TCP 和 TLS 都成功，但证书是 `*.facebook.com`”，和根因一致：请求没走 magpie 自己的代理设置（或系统代理），直接出去了，握手对象是投毒后的解析。`v0.1.1686` 之后客户端 `t.Proxy = netproxy.Func`（magpie 里设置的代理，其次系统代理），和 magpie 其它请求一个路。
- 你的两个模型命运不同：`AstrLink Guard` 在修复后还多了一条 hf-mirror 的后备源（上游对真实镜像核过三个文件的 sha256）；`Privacy Filter` 的 GGUF 则 hf-mirror 会 308 重定向回 huggingface.co，所以它的出路仍然是你把代理填进 Settings → Proxy，让下载走 `CONNECT`。
- 等待版本：tag `v0.1.1686` 已含修复，release 一发布（或之后的任何版本）就带上它；`v0.1.1685` 及更早都没有。

顺带交代我们这条线：#3561 最初报的初始化顺序 bug，我们 fork 上的 `fix/pii-download-proxy`（`55dfe0a5`）和上游的修法等价（同样的 `t.Proxy = netproxy.Func` + `netproxy.Dispatch`），上游独立落地了它自己的版本（还多了镜像后备），所以这条分支就不再追了，以 main 的 `3a89dd53` 为准。

Fixed on `fix/3561-privacy-model-proxy` (8f20732e467648a893ad57e1ea3e83764ef1d635):

The pf-serve and local model downloads in `internal/pii/fetch.go` used a
package-level `http.Client` created at init time, before `netproxy.Install()`
wired the proxy function. The client's transport was cloned from
`http.DefaultTransport` before the settings proxy was wired, so downloads
went direct even when a proxy was configured in Settings.

Fix: `clientFactory` is now a function called for each download, so the
current proxy settings (via `netproxy.Func`) are always used. Tests updated
to override `clientFactory` for mocking.

Test: `TestFetchGoesThroughMagpiesProxy` verifies the download goes
through the configured proxy. All pii tests pass (56 passed).
